rows.text: It's been thirty years since we last saw each other, right, Yukong?
rows.speaker: Feixiao

rows.text: Yes, back then, you were the vanguard at the Yaoqing's Verdant Knights, and I was a pilot of the Luofu's Rainbowfall Fleet. Who would have thought that upon meeting again, you'd be a general, and I'd have given up flying... Really does feel like a lifetime ago.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: Heh, don't mention it. Thank you for taking the time to welcome me.
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: General, I've brought our guests from the Express. I'm sorry for my bad timing. I didn't know you were meeting a guest, General.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Don't worry. You're just in time. It's been a while, my friends from the Astral Express!
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: All is well when you have friends coming from afar.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Oh? Well It's an honor to be in your dreams, my friend.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Glad to meet you, Miss Yunli.
Sure, how couldn't I have? It's not often we find such moments to reunite and enjoy one another's presence.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: What's the "Flamewheel Octet" the general spoke of?
Since when did [Trailblazer] and General Jing Yuan become such good buddies, Dan Heng? They seem to be having a great time.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Aren't you coming with us?
A lot must have happened without our knowledge. At least I hope that's the case...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I'm just a tourist attending the ceremony.
Allow me to introduce you to General Huaiyan. He's the Arbiter-General of the Xianzhou Zhuming, known as the Flaming Heart.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Can outsiders participate in the Wardance as well?
Hehe, no need to be so formal. I'm just a tourist here, no different from other tourists who've come to attend the ceremony.
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: He shouldn't have said you "stole" his sword.

Elder Huaiyan is not only one of the Arbiter-Generals but also the Furnace Master of the Artisanship Commission. Besides his martial skills, he excels in forging various weapons. Such talents are unique, even among the Arbiter-Generals.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: But you did take his sword...
There appears to be more than meets the eye.

Be it Arbiter-General or Furnace Master, these are merely titles given to me long ago. I've retired several times already, but with the current change in circumstances, the Marshal has called me back to duty, and I had no choice but to answer the call.
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: Why does he look so old?
Well, in the end, I'm to blame. Living such a long life naturally brings its share of disapproval.
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: Perhaps he's a robot.
It's an honor to meet you, General Huaiyan.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng & Yanqing

rows.text: It's my honor to meet you, General Huaiyan...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Is this some kind of test from the general?
No need to be all formal. Today I'm just a guest on the Luofu, the same as all of you.
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: Let's go.
Not yet.
I'll go get it back for you.
So, these three are the ones you mentioned, Jing Yuan? The heroes who helped you with the Ambrosial Arbor Crisis?
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: I don't think you'll ever get your sword back!
Indeed. There's Dan Heng, March 7th, and [Trailblazer]... Without their help, I'm afraid the Luofu might not have easily overcome this crisis.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: So, the Imbibitor Lunae's reincarnation has returned to the Luofu and will attend the Wardance. I'd love to have a drink with you should the chance presents itself.
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: We can vouch for Jing Yuan, though.
You're more than welcome, General Huaiyan.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: No wonder we were called back for the ceremony.
And this young friend is...?
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: You're a real master of conversation!

Yanqing, my apprentice. He remains by my side as my retainer due to his youth, which I hope will season him with experience. He will stand for the Luofu's Cloud Knights in the upcoming Wardance, ready to take on all kinds of challenges.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Please, March, just keep quiet.
Brag all you want, but don't drag me into this.
Great, great! It's a real treat to see so many talented young people around here today.
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: You're a real master of conversation!
Oh, I almost forgot... This is my apprentice, Yunli...
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: Stop, stop! I don't want to end up in an IPC lawsuit.
It's you!
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Oh, it's you. Hello.
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: How's everything going, General?
Oh, you two already know each other? Guess we don't need any introductions then!
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: I dreamed about you on Penacony.
What a coincidence! I was afraid I'd have trouble finding this girl.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Did you miss us?
Oh? Now you've piqued my curiosity... Tell me, how did you two become acquainted?
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: She helped me capture the escaped borisin prisoners at the Starskiff Haven. Allow me to express my gratitude for you, but when you left... you took my Flying Sword with you.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Glad to meet you, General.
Your Flying Sword?... Oh, so that's why I found a dagger in my bag. Turns out it's yours.
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: Yes, it is. Now that we've met again, I hope...
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Nope, that won't do.
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: Won't do?
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: You want your sword back, right? Well, you can't just take it back. On the Zhuming, when you lose your sword on the battlefield, you have to reclaim it on the battlefield.
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: As for this little sword, it was supposed to strike that escaped borisin prisoner, but unfortunately its owner's agitated state caused it to fly off like a kite with a broken string, and it missed its target.
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: By the way, if I hadn't caught it and helped it hit its mark, that borisin prisoner would have gotten away.
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: Hold on a sec, Yunli. You took my sword without even asking, and now you're refusing to give it back?
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: ...Heh, so much for Luofu swordmasters.
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: What did you just say?
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: If you just stepped up and took your sword back from me fair and square, I would have totally respected you. But nope, you tried to play it down, expecting me to just hand it back to you like it's nothing, in front of everyone...
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: With all due respect, you don't honor your sword, so you don't deserve it.
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: Hasn't anyone told you that taking without asking is stealing? If you want to settle this with swords... Fine, let's have a one-on-one duel right now...
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Yanqing.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Well, that's more like it. Just be careful, because I'm not as easy to handle as the borisin.
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: You too. Be quiet and apologize to Yanqing!
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: Hey, whose side are you on, Grandpa?
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: I... um... I don't take sides!
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: It's a small misunderstanding, and an apology would be too much. I've heard about the Zhuming's incredible swordplay and craftsmanship, most notably the legendary Flamewheel Octet. Seeing Miss Yunli, who is among those ranks today... Well I must say, she definitely has that fiery edge.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: ...Such grandiose names. Some folks love to spin these fancy titles, trying to set the Cloud Knights apart. Yunli is still just a young girl, a bit awkward and hot-tempered. So please forgive her if she's being rude.
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: Well, everyone, Elder Huaiyan and I have some business to discuss. For now, Yanqing, why don't you entertain our guests and take Miss Yunli to the inn?
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: I'll find another chance to talk with you all. I'd like to express my gratitude to the Astral Express for helping the Luofu during the crisis.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: That's so kind of you. I mean you've already thanked us so many times.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Please forgive me for coming at an inconvenient time.
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: You needn't apologize, General Huaiyan.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Alright, Yunli. Take this opportunity to clear things up with Yanqing.
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: Yeah, yeah, it's better to make friends than enemies, but I won't be heading to the inn just yet... I want to visit Lingsha. She just arrived in the Luofu and could use some help settling in.
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: Yanqing, once you've helped our guests get settled, go to the Artisanship Commission for me. I've heard about the attack and the detainment of the IPC ship. Qingzu sent word that the IPC members are protesting and wish to have their cargo back.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: See if you can calm them down. Don't get aggressive. Just make it clear that the Xianzhou Luofu has no intention of violating their rights.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: I'm on it.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Glad to meet you, too. Are you here to participate in the Wardance?
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: So, you're not a participant? You look like you know your way around a fight.
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: Of course. To honor martial arts, the Cloud Knights' ring is always open to outsiders.
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: That's how outsiders refer to my peers in the Zhuming Cloud Knights and the Artisanship Commission.
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: I have some things to do. Besides, little Yanqing doesn't seem too happy about me tagging along.
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: You're right. I "took" it with my skills, so I guess you can say I'm a robber or something. How dare he imply I'm a thief. Totally different!
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: In the meantime, outside the Palace of Astrum...
I'm sorry for Yanqing's rudeness.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Not at all. Taunted by Yunli like that, even a training dummy would be angry. You've taught your apprentice well. If it were me in my younger days, I'm afraid I'd have drawn my sword and fought.
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: Yanqing can understand your concerns. On the other hand, Yunli is still a naive girl who's only interested in swordplay. Honestly, I brought her here to participate in the Wardance because I want to broaden her horizons.
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: Don't you find it strange, [Trailblazer]? Do Xianzhou people age? I rarely see any old people on the Xianzhou ship, and when I do, they're usually travelers.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Yeah, you've noticed that too. It's really weird... Do the Xianzhou people age? I rarely see any old people on the Xianzhou ship, and when I do, they're usually travelers.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Like Madam Herta? Hmmm, that would make sense. Anyway, it's really weird for a Xianzhou native to look so old.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Good question. He's right there, so why don't you ask him yourself?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Well, it's not exactly a "test." As Cloud Knight officers, we not only learn the art of war and martial arts but also occasionally have to handle diplomatic disputes.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Well, let's not worry about that for now. Shall I take you to the inn?
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: It is the Luofu's honor to have you in attendance at the Wardance.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Yet, the fact that a simple martial arts ceremony has attracted esteemed generals from the Zhuming and the Yaoqing implies intentions beyond mere spectating. Might there be any specific instructions from the Marshal?
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: You're overthinking it, Jing Yuan. As I said, I'm here to broaden my granddaughter's horizons. I have no ulterior motives.
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: However, I have no clue what the Yaoqing Arbiter-General has in mind.
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: Do you remember when you accepted this position? I told you that an Arbiter-General's battlefield goes beyond the physical one. You'll need to lead and manage everything on the Xianzhou... The title of Arbiter-General holds a weight far greater than its literal meaning.
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: So many years have passed, and you've done well. However, longevity for the Xianzhou people can be a curse. Living too long means that every mistake you made will lurk in the shadows, and one day, they'll eventually catch up to you.
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: The Marshal knows {RUBY_B#The ins and outs of the Ambrosial Arbor Disaster}everything that has happened on the Luofu{RUBY_E#}. As for the Merlin's Claw of the Yaoqing...
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: ...She has come specifically for you.
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: Speaking of which, why hasn't she arrived yet? They say the Merlin's Claw strikes like lightning. Being late isn't her style.
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: That's not true, General Huaiyan. She's been here a while, but I'm sure you've heard of her unbridled nature.
As soon as she disembarked from the starskiff, she mentioned having something to attend to and simply disappeared.
You must be the messengers from the Xianzhou Yaoqing, I assume.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: We are Jiaoqiu and Moze, retainers of the Merlin's Claw. It's an honor to meet you in person, Arbiter-Generals.
Now, this is interesting. A guest who doesn't come to visit but sends a message instead. What does she mean? Tell me, what could be more important to her than coming here?
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: Master heard about a spectacular view in Scalegorge Waterscape. I believe she went there to enjoy it.
rows.speaker: Jiaoqiu

rows.text: A "spectacular" view? Hah! Did you hear that, Jing Yuan? This person is being sarcastic.
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: Please do not misunderstand me, General Huaiyan. I was simply stating the truth. Master thought it would be inappropriate to keep you waiting, so she sent us here...
rows.speaker: Jiaoqiu

rows.text: Once she's finished with admiring the scenery, she'll personally come and apologize to the both of you.
rows.speaker: Jiaoqiu

rows.text: Drat, I forgot to ask Yunli to return my sword...
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: No need to bother. The Zhuming envoys won't be leaving the Luofu anytime soon. I'll ask for it later when we meet again.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Unacceptable! Every sword is precious to me!
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: If it weren't for the general's interference, I would have taught that shameless girl a lesson in swordplay...
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: By the way, I don't know if it's just me, but the general seemed a little... hmmm, reserved? Could it be because of Elder Huaiyan's visit?
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Reserved? Really?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Maybe I'm just overthinking things.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: No, you're not. When I entered the Palace of Astrum, I realized that the messenger from the Xianzhou Zhuming was actually the Arbiter-General himself. So, the messenger from the Xianzhou Yaoqing must be the Merlin's Claw herself, I presume?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: That's right.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: That's what makes this entire thing so unusual.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: What's so unusual about it? They simply received an invitation from Jing Yuan, just like the Crew, right?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The Wardance is just a small festival, and now we have two Arbiter-Generals from other Xianzhou ships here. I'm afraid they're here for something more.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Maybe they've come to hold Jing Yuan accountable for the Ambrosial Arbor Crisis?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Hold him accountable? Come on, didn't the Luofu fall victim to the Disciples of Sanctus Medicus and the Antimatter Legion? Why would they blame the victim?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Dan Shu's rebellion and Phantylia's scheming are merely one side of the story to the other Arbiter-Generals of the Alliance. Only a single piece of incontrovertible evidence remains, creating an endless source of potential complications.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: The Ambrosial Arbor.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Yes, it's undeniable that the plaguemark, which was subdued by the Xianzhou Luofu, has resurfaced. But was it really a conspiracy instigated by the Antimatter Legion, or does it indicate a traitorous intent from within the Luofu, implicating Jing Yuan himself?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Once the spark of suspicion is kindled, it proves hard to extinguish.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: The general must have had that in mind when he invited us to attend the Wardance.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: After watching Yanqing and the others leave...
What was I thinking, seriously. Here I was looking forward to a carefree and enjoyable trip, but it seems wherever we go, drama is just around the corner.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Aww... I was so excited. I thought those Arbiter-Generals were just here to see the ceremony...
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: By the way, I heard that an alchemist from the Zhuming diplomatic ship has arrived, and rumors say that she's to be the new Cauldron Master of the Alchemy Commission on the Luofu.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: An alchemist from the Zhuming serving as the Cauldron Master on the Luofu? While it's not unheard of, the timing itself...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Thanks to your words, Mr. Dan Heng, now I finally see the underlying tensions.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: The general is under tremendous pressure right now, but I was completely oblivious to his troubles... How naive of me!
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Come on! Don't think like that! Leave the adult matters to the adults. Even if you wanted to do something for the general, it's not like you can do anything.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Uh, did I say something wrong again?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Miss March is right. I don't have the skills to share the general's burdens at the moment.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: ...Still, I'll do my best to follow his instructions. Let's go. Once I've taken you to your accommodations, I need to go to the Artisanship Commission to handle the IPC's protest.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: He looks like he has a lot on his mind. We can't just let him go alone... Why don't we accompany you to the Artisanship Commission?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: This... is too much trouble. While I appreciate your kindness, dealing with the IPC workers could be tricky... I'm afraid this will cause trouble for the Express...
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: No worries! We're pretty experienced in dealing with the IPC! You've heard of the Ten Stonehearts, right? We've dealt with quite a few of them, right, [Trailblazer]?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hey, who's bragging? Anyway, this time it's just a few ordinary IPC workers. Surely you don't think they'll be even trickier than Aventurine, do you?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Yeah, exactly... Uhm, are you being sarcastic?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: What's with you turning into a scaredy-cat? I didn't see you worrying about lawsuits when you wrecked that giant mech.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Well, since you're willing to help, I won't decline your kindness. Let's head to the Artisanship Commission and meet them.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Can I really reason with you Xianzhou people?
Heh, I think I get it now. In your words, this is called "looting a burning house," right?
But I AM trying to reason with you here!
rows.speaker: Xikui

rows.text: (That toxic voice sounds familiar... Haven't I heard it before in Aurum Alley?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: You know what? This isn't my first time dealing with the Sky-Faring Commission, I can handle your unreasonable ways.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: But straight-up snatching IPC cargo, isn't that going a bit too far?
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Just as I've said it many times already. Once we've inspected the cargo and completed the security check, you can be on your way. Is there something wrong with your ears, or is it just your brain?
rows.speaker: Kongqing

rows.text: I'm hearing you loud and clear! I'm thinking clear! And my answer is crystal clear: Not a chance!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Keep detaining my cargo, and I'll file a complaint directly with your general!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Don't think you can possibly convince me! Uh huh!? Why are you here!?
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: I was gonna ask you the same thing! Why do I keep running into you!?
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: You jerk! Who are you calling a "dog?" Wait... wh—why are you here!?
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: You're staying on the Xianzhou, are you? What terrible luck. Wherever you go, disasters aren't far behind...
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Aren't you the guests from the Astral Express? What brings you and Yanqing to the Artisanship Commission?
rows.speaker: Xikui

rows.text: They're in trouble? No, it's me! I'm the one in trouble!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Trouble caused by the IPC? I'd say it's caused by the Sky-Faring Commission!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Looks like you've met this IPC worker before, [Trailblazer]... I'm not sure if that's a good or bad thing.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: I was sent here to deal with the IPC protest, Miss Xikui. What's going on here?
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: As you know, this IPC transport ship was attacked by the borisin and rescued by the Zhuming's diplomatic ship. Then the Cloud Knights were instructed to bring it back to the dock for repairs and inspections.
rows.speaker: Xikui

rows.text: And this is Mr. Skott, the person in charge of this transport ship.
rows.speaker: Xikui

rows.text: So, you're Skott! I've heard [Trailblazer] mention you! Weren't you kicked off the Luofu before? Why did you come back?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Like I wanted to come back! I thought I'd just dock at the harbor for repairs and leave this forsaken place for good. Little did I know, as soon as the ship entered the harbor, a bunch of Cloud Knights showed up and snatched all our cargo from the hold!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: What do you mean by "snatched"? I've told you a million times. It's a security check.
rows.speaker: Xikui

rows.text: Then why did you bring the cargo to the Artisanship Commission? You even brought in some shady craftsman. It's obvious that you're trying to steal the IPC's patented technology!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Listen here... Firstly, the Sky-Faring Commission detected dangerous items that could possibly be weapons in your cargo hold, that's why they called me here to double-check. Secondly, where the heck did you get the idea that I'm a "shady craftsman"!?
rows.speaker: Kongqing

rows.text: Even if there are dangerous items, what do they have to do with you? It's not even being shipped to the Luofu. We'll just fix the ship and be on our way, we won't unload our cargo here.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: But you'll have to stay in the port for several days before your ship is repaired and you can take off again. How can we just leave unchecked items sitting here?
rows.speaker: Xikui

rows.text: I understand... but we don't need to disassemble the cargo if it's just a security check, right?
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: In most cases, we don't. However, our scans discovered that the cargo doesn't only contain machinery but also some... substance that resembles biological tissue.
rows.speaker: Kongqing

rows.text: Biological tissue? Does this crate contain living things?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I'm afraid we'll need to wait for the Alchemy Commission for further confirmation. In any case, according to our regulations, we need to unseal one of the crates for further examination, but this IPC specialist has been hindering us on the grounds of patent secrecy.
rows.speaker: Kongqing

rows.text: Well, honestly, at least you're not as annoying as that woman.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Well, honestly, at least you're not as annoying as that woman.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Well, honestly, at least you're not as annoying as that woman.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: The Alliance's regulations on biological products are very strict. Without further inspection, there is no way for the Sky-Faring Commission to release the cargo.
rows.speaker: Xikui

rows.text: Oh, really? Fine! If anyone lays a finger on that shipment, they'll have me to deal with! It doesn't matter if it's mechanical or biological, it's none of your business! I'm filing a complaint against the Sky-Faring Commission's ridiculous regulations!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: This Mr. Skott seems stubborn and difficult to persuade. Honestly... I really don't want to have a vicious confrontation with the IPC...
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: I heard how you helped Aurum Alley, [Trailblazer]. The IPC representative back then was Mr. Skott, right? Since you've dealt with him before... it looks like I'll have to rely on you again, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: What are you guys whispering about over there? Just hurry up and give us back our cargo!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: The Alliance can sign a non-disclosure agreement with you. That way, you won't have to worry about any infringements, right?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I didn't expect to see you again, Mr. Skott! We had such fun in Aurum Alley last time. It seems our paths are destined to cross once more.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Back in Aurum Alley, you were dealing with civilian merchants, where you could use the IPC's name to scare them.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Hey, everyone! Meet my old friend, Skott. He's very talented, especially at imitating animals.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I've got a brilliant idea! I'll just smash everything with my bat, and then you can hire someone to assess the damage. That way, your cargo won't need any inspection, right?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Don't underestimate Xianzhou technology. Even if they need to dismantle your cargo, the Artisanship Commission can easily put it back together.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Hah! I've taken Herta's curios, and even destroyed Ruan Mei's experimental subjects, but have I ever paid a penny for them? And now you think you can just come and ask me for compensation?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Can you give us an exact amount, Mr. Skott? If there's any damage after the inspection, the Express... um, I mean, the Sky-Faring Commission will compensate you.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I'm pretty tight with Dr. Ratio from the Intelligentsia Guild, almost like family. Doesn't that make me practically a member of the Intelligentsia Guild too?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: You're pulling out all the stops, and you've even dragged members of the Intelligentsia Guild into this. Seems like you're not interested in resolving this at all.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: According to the principle of territoriality, since your vessel is stranded on the Xianzhou, the Sky-Faring Commission has the right to inspect it.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Since the Intelligentsia Guild entrusted the cargo to the IPC for transportation, it's the IPC's responsibility to ensure its safety, right? Why would you need a member of the Intelligentsia Guild to be present?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Everyone has their own set of rules. Now that you're on their turf, shouldn't you follow their rules, too?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: How about this, pal? We go way back... so, if you make things easy for us today, we'll make it worth your while. What do you say?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I understand that you're trying to stick to the IPC regulations, and that's commendable, Mr. Skott. But what you fail to see is that this argument is tarnishing the IPC's reputation on the Xianzhou.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Please, help me! I mean it! I bragged to my friends that I could convince you... If you don't do me this favor, I'll be so embarrassed! Come on, don't be so cold-hearted!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Well, you guys sure know how to argue your case...
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Fine! I'll allow you to do the security inspection. It's just that... I need some time to sort things out. This is a big deal. Let me talk to headquarters first.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Well, IPC staff are free to come and go, as long as they don't break any laws.
Yeah, you've got some insight there. Who are you again?
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Alright, that's enough. I'm not going to repeat myself a hundred times.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: I thought you were reasonable and civilized, but now it seems you Xianzhou folks just don't understand the basics of business.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: We've signed a confidentiality and security agreement with the Intelligentsia Guild, and if we breach it, we'll have to pay a hefty sum! Even if we sold the souls of every employee in the Marketing Development Department on this planet, it still wouldn't be enough to cover the costs.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Listen up, kid. I don't mind delaying this transport for a few more days. Once the engines are repaired, our ship will leave immediately, and you won't have any reason to inspect the cargo.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: So, Mr. Skott, are you just stalling for time, and planning to leave the Xianzhou as soon as your ship is repaired to avoid the Sky-Faring Commission's inspection?
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: If that's the case, I can assure you the Cloud Knights won't let your ship leave.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Oh, really? Then you'll receive a ton of complaints from the Intelligentsia Guild and the IPC's Marketing Development Department. You're too young, I don't think you understand the chaos your rash decision will cause.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Since you put it that way, Mr. Skott, I'll take it as your agreement to the inspection procedure. Now...
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Not so fast, you little brat. According to the IPC regulations, I have the right to arm myself and protect the property on my transport ship.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: I thought you were reasonable and civilized, but now it seems the IPC just wants to play by its own rules. My apologies, Mr. Skott.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Stop him, guys! For the Amber Lord!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: For the Amber Lord!!!
rows.speaker: IPC Staff Members

rows.text: Get up, all of you! Why is the IPC even paying you? You're a bunch of losers!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Just be grateful that the "little brat" showed you mercy. At least your staff aren't seriously injured.
How do you IPC cronies have the audacity to fight Cloud Knights...? You practically assaulted law enforcement officers.
Another one? Who the heck are you!?
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: I may be a bit late, but the good news is: I'm here now.
Allow me to introduce myself. I'm Lingsha, Cauldron Master and Head of the Alchemy Commission on the Luofu.
Could she be...?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Yeah, she's the new Cauldron Master assigned here from the Xianzhou Zhuming.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: I received a report from the Artisanship Commission about cargo containing samples of unknown organisms. It said they needed help from the Alchemy Commission. I had nothing better to do, so I came myself.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: It's fine, Mr. Skott. If you really don't want your cargo to be inspected, it doesn't matter.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: It doesn't matter? How can you say that?
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Why are you being so nice all of a sudden? Well, since you're not going to check it, I'll take this crate and be on my way. Is that okay with everyone?
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Yeah, sure. Why should I object? Not only this sample, but all the goods on the transport ship are yours to keep. Like I said, we won't inspect them.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: Wait a minute!
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Well, that's more like it! If only the young displayed a more... reasonable attitude, we could have sidestepped that altercation just now.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Our ship will leave in a few days once the engines are repaired.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Your ship can leave whenever you want, but I'm afraid I can't say the same for the cargo.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: According to the import and export regulations signed between the Xianzhou and IPC, all biological shipments can only leave the port when they have confirmed to be of no threat, or when all biological activity expires.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: Since we can't determine if your shipment is safe for the environment, I guess we'll have to wait for its biological activity to expire. Let me check the previous cases...
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: Normally it'll only take around forty-seven star calendar years.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: "Only" forty-seven years?
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Why so surprised? You're still young and full of energy. I'm pretty sure you'll live a few more decades. Have some confidence in yourself!
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: Typical of a long-life species, your words are dripping with sarcasm. While you may not care about time, I do! I'll be demanding double compensation from the Sky-Faring Commission for every minute wasted!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Sure thing, Mr. Skott. You seem pretty confident that your career and life will last long enough to witness this victory unfold.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: Step aside, guys. Let them do the inspection.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: But Mr. Skott...
rows.speaker: IPC Worker

rows.text: Come on, we're already in enough trouble... Just let them do the security inspection. And if needed, I can always grovel before the Intelligentsia Guild later — I'm just using my head for what it's apparently good for, right?
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: But you're still as annoying as ever.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: "Bro?" Just do the inspection!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Just get on with the inspection! Don't act all chummy with me now that you've got your way.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: This lady... is really something else!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Were you seriously planning to leave this stuff unchecked at the dock for days? That's way too dangerous!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I... I had no idea about it! You must have accidentally triggered the cargo's defense program!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: I don't think trying to shift the blame is a wise choice.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: But seriously, I don't know why that thing suddenly started moving...! I swear on the Amber Lord!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Enough. Miss Xikui, please escort our IPC guests to the Sky-Faring Commission.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: I'm on it. Please follow me, Mr. Skott.
rows.speaker: Xikui

rows.text: Our preliminary inspection shows that there is indeed hidden biological tissues inside, just like the craftsman feared.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: I can't even tell if it's ingenium or biological in nature.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: The core of this device is what they call "wetware" in industry slang. To put it simply, this machine operates with a kind of biological nerve as its control center.
rows.speaker: Kongqing

rows.text: I'll take some samples for the alchemists to analyze and figure out where the biological tissue comes from.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: Why would the Intelligentsia Guild use such unethical technology? Perhaps they are trying to create a new weapon?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Whatever the reason is, it's probably why the borisin attacked the ship.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: No wonder the IPC were trying to obstruct our inspection. I'll contact the Ten-Lords Commission and ask the judges to come and give their final verdict on this.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: According to our rules, all prisoners and weapons involving dangerous creatures must be taken to The Shackling Prison for further sentencing. After all, it's the safest place on the Luofu.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: As for you, Mr. craftsman, please go with the Cloud Knights and explain the situation to the judge.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: I had a feeling that the IPC members would cause trouble, but I didn't think they'd be this tricky. Thanks for your help, Miss Lingsha.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: I should thank you for saving my life. Your sword skills were impressive, taking down that big guy.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: I thought the General's retainers were all burly martial masters. I didn't expect Yanqing to be so...
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: Yeah, exactly. He's young and talented.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: Hmm, can't argue with that.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: Huh???
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: As for you, you must be the guests from the Astral Express, right? Saving the Luofu from that crisis, it's so impressive.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: Hehe, it wasn't a big deal, really...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It's still early, so why don't we get some tea at the Alchemy Commission? We can discuss your suggestions for revitalizing the commission.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: I'd be happy to accept your invitation.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: And you three are coming too, right?
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: After a while, everyone disperses and goes their own way...

There you are, Master Lingsha. Just a reminder, the Alchemy Commission on the Luofu has always had a close relationship with the Preceptors, so avoiding a meeting like this doesn't align with our long-standing practices...
rows.speaker: Yuluo

rows.text: Practices? Come on, you make it sound like the "long-standing practices" in this Alchemy Commission are something great.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: You're right, Cauldron Master. In this case... I'll continue handling them on your behalf.
rows.speaker: Yuluo

rows.text: Thank you for your help.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: Do you have any idea how many years I've waited just to see the Healer Lady? And now someone cuts in line? How is that fair?
rows.speaker: Angry Patient

rows.text: Please calm down... That person is an esteemed guest who has traveled from afar. She simply couldn't wait in line for years, so we had to let her see the Healer Lady before you.
rows.speaker: Resigned Medic

rows.text: But don't worry. As soon as she's done, it'll be your turn. By the way, the esteemed guest said she'll cover your medical expenses as compensation.
rows.speaker: Resigned Medic

rows.text: Well... I guess that's acceptable. Your "esteemed guest" seems reasonable, so I'll just pretend nothing happened.
rows.speaker: Angry Patient

rows.text: Thanks for understanding. Please have a rest over here.
rows.speaker: Resigned Medic

rows.text: Are you all ready?
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: Let's do it!
Let's wait a moment.
I'm here to pay my respects to the new Cauldron Master.
rows.speaker: Preceptor Servant

rows.text: Cauldron Master Lingsha is busy with official business...
rows.speaker: Yuluo

rows.text: Cut it out. I'm carrying out my sacred duty.
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: Because of someone important. So, stop asking and be serious. I'm on duty right now.
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: Yeah, see you later.
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: Stop hanging around here and find something better to do. Once I'm done in a few days, call up Lil Gui and Huohuo, and let's grab a meal at Aurum Alley. It's been ages since we hung out.
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: My bad. Well, since you went through the entire Ambrosial Arbor Crisis firsthand, Dan Heng and Lieutenant Yanqing, I'd like to discuss something with you.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: But which general should I call?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Between these two, who do you think is tougher? Don't get me wrong, I'm just curious.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Between these two, who do you think is tougher, Dan Heng? Don't get me wrong, I'm just curious.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It is my first day at the Alchemy Commission — a brawl is definitely not how I imagined celebrating it.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: I'm Shehong, a messenger sent by Preceptor Taoran. He wanted to come and congratulate his kindred on becoming Cauldron Master personally, but health limitations hindered his visit.
rows.speaker: Shehong

rows.text: So, I'm here to pay my respects to the Cauldron Master on his behalf. Could you let her know about my arrival, dear chief alchemist?
rows.speaker: Shehong

rows.text: Master Lingsha just arrived on the Luofu and is still settling in and getting her work in order. She's quite busy and unable to meet guests right now. Please understand.
rows.speaker: Yuluo

rows.text: Well then... Please pass this humble gift on to her.
rows.speaker: Shehong

rows.text: I'm pretty sure this "humble gift" from the Preceptor himself is quite valuable. As a mere chief alchemist, I am unable to deliver it. Should any mishap occur, I couldn't bear the consequences.
rows.speaker: Yuluo

rows.text: I see. So when will I be able to see Master Lingsha?
rows.speaker: Shehong

rows.text: I'm not sure. Whenever Master Lingsha feels it is appropriate, she will most certainly get in touch with you.
rows.speaker: Yuluo

rows.text: Then I shall wait with anticipation.
rows.speaker: Shehong

rows.text: All these years, and the view at the Alchemy Commission hasn't changed a bit.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: The tides come and go, but the ancient sea remains the same. For us Vidyadhara, there's nothing more nostalgic than our homeland.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: ...You're a Luofu native, Miss Lingsha?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Yes, I grew up here, listening to the sound of waves while researching prescriptions with my mentors and peers at the Alchemy Commission.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: It's kind of sad, isn't it? Everything changes but somehow remains familiar. Just like you, Dan Heng, I traveled far from home, and now I've returned. Seeing the familiar scenery brings back a hint of nostalgia.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: The view here would be even better without the Ambrosial Arbor.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Oh, really? I think that towering tree looks pretty impressive.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: Even if it's impressive, it's a plaguemark. The Xianzhou have been fighting abominations for thousands of years, and now that the Ambrosial Arbor has been reborn, it's only natural for everyone to feel uneasy.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Well, once a seed is planted, no matter how long it takes, it'll eventually sprout and bear fruit.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: In my humble opinion, the rebirth of the Ambrosial Arbor and the resurgence of the Disciples of Sanctus Medicus were inevitable. The seed was already planted when the ancestors of the Xianzhou sought immortality.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: What would you like to discuss, Miss Lingsha?
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: I was lucky enough to be chosen by the Alliance to come in and clean up all the old grime in the Alchemy Commission.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: Honestly, the Alchemy Commission is riddled with problems and has reached a point where fixing it seems impossible. I'm looking to "remedy" this problem, but was wondering if you could provide any insights?
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: Well, even though I'm a Vidyadharan like you, I'm an outsider just like my companions here. I can't really say much about a "remedy," but... I do have a piece of advice, Miss Lingsha.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: The Vidyadhara and the Alchemy Commission on the Luofu have always been intricately connected. If you cannot distance yourself from these ties, Miss Lingsha, changing the situation within the Alchemy Commission may be quite challenging.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I may not know about politics, but I do know that the Disciples of Sanctus Medicus have been operating within the Alchemy Commission for years. If you're determined to root them out, maybe you should discuss it with the general.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: I see. Thank you for your valuable insights.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: While the Lux Arrow from the Reignbow possesses unparalleled power to sever the Ambrosial Arbor, it can't sever mortals' desire to prolong their existence.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: Just like how the Cloud Knights can eliminate the remnants of the Disciples of Sanctus Medicus, but are unable to calm the hearts and minds of the people within the Alchemy Commission.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: Our Xianzhou forbears knew this well, and that's why they entrusted the duty of guarding the Roots of the Arbor to the Vidyadhara. However, the Vidyadhara are still only mortal beings.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: Thirty years ago, my mentor served as Alchemy Commission's Cauldron Master. She recognized the emerging undercurrents and sought to cleanse the source of the disturbance.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: Unfortunately, even though she was skilled in the art of healing, she didn't understand the human heart or how to eliminate the sickness lurking within the depths of the Alchemy Commission. In the end, she was framed and exiled to the Zhuming. I was also implicated and had to leave the Luofu.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: And guess who arbitrated that case and handed down the sentence...? None other than General Jing Yuan himself.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: Wh—What!?
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: You heard it right. The ones responsible for the corruption in the Alchemy Commission are not just the remnants of the Disciples of Sanctus Medicus, but even the Divine Foresight himself.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: Alas, why is your face turning pale, Yanqing?
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: Don't worry about it. I understand that when someone holds a position of power, they may sometimes have to make tough decisions. I won't hold any personal grudges against him. Besides, at our age, holding personal grudges is a luxury we can't afford.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: Lingsha, you're back! I've been waiting ages for you!
Yunli? Why aren't you with your grandpa? What brings you to the Alchemy Commission?
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: Well, let me take this opportunity to introduce you to Yanqing...
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: What a small world...
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: You...! You stole my sword! Give it back!
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: I see. Let's skip the "introduction" part then.
rows.speaker: Lingsha

rows.text: Back already? You've met with Jing Yuan and wandered around for a few hours. So, what do you think?
rows.speaker: Feixiao

rows.text: It appears that the Divine Foresight is using this Wardance as a show of strength to convince everyone that the Luofu is prospering after the Ambrosial Arbor Crisis...
rows.speaker: Jiaoqiu

rows.text: But... I know you're going to say "But," right?
rows.speaker: Feixiao

rows.text: But, the influx of people attending the Wardance is like a breeding ground for disorder and rumors. One wrong move, and the Luofu could be in a world of chaos.
rows.speaker: Jiaoqiu

rows.text: The Cloud Knights on the streets remain vigilant, so at the very least General Jing Yuan is aware of this. As for other matters, I'm unable to say.
rows.speaker: Moze

rows.text: I'd prefer to be excused from future meetings with generals. I'm just a military healer, and now all of a sudden I'm thrust onto the center stage having cordial chats with two generals?
rows.speaker: Jiaoqiu

rows.text: My work doesn't lend itself to being in the limelight, either.
rows.speaker: Moze

rows.text: Just stop whining. At least you're in one piece, right?
rows.speaker: Feixiao

rows.text: Before getting in touch with General Jing Yuan, I want to put aside my assumptions and see his "momentum." That includes the overall bearing of the Cloud Knights on the street, what people are saying, and how those close to him behave.
rows.speaker: Feixiao

rows.text: "The might of an army dwells not within its pawns, but within the force of its collective momentum. Recognizing this fact reveals the true measure of power." Thanks for enlightening me, General.
rows.speaker: Jiaoqiu

rows.text: A perfectly clear statement turned confusing thanks to your translation — you've made me lose where I was now. Anyway, this is how I operate in battle, so you might as well get used to it.
rows.speaker: Feixiao

rows.text: Are you treating General Jing Yuan as your enemy?
rows.speaker: Jiaoqiu

rows.text: The longest-serving general of the Xianzhou Luofu. Do you think he'd have only a few enemies?
rows.speaker: Feixiao

rows.text: By the way, General, you met the Healer Lady, yes? Could you show me the medicine she prescribed you?
rows.speaker: Jiaoqiu

rows.text: Well, the Healer Lady couldn't do anything about my condition. She just told me to "enjoy some tasty food."
rows.speaker: Feixiao

rows.text: ...So, not even the famed Healer Lady could help?
rows.speaker: Jiaoqiu

rows.text: Don't worry. I'll fulfill my promise and find a way to cure you. Actually, I've found some leads.
rows.speaker: Jiaoqiu

rows.text: Well, life and death, Jiaoqiu, it's all predetermined.
rows.speaker: Feixiao

rows.text: Upon starting my military career, I made a pledge that the rest of my life would be dedicated to being the Xianzhou's spearhead, hunting down the Abominations of Abundance till the end of my days.
rows.speaker: Feixiao

rows.text: As long as I can fulfill that deep-seated desire... I don't care how long I live.
rows.speaker: Feixiao

rows.text: You asked if I view General Jing Yuan as my enemy... No, my real enemy has always been myself.
rows.speaker: Feixiao

rows.text: "Enjoy some tasty food" So... what's for dinner tonight?
rows.speaker: Moze

rows.text: Geez... you really know how to read the room, don't you?
rows.speaker: Jiaoqiu

rows.text: You guys figure it out for yourselves. I'm due to catch up with an old war friend I've not seen for quite a long time.
rows.speaker: Feixiao

rows.text: Meanwhile, Yanqing and [Trailblazer] return to the Exalting Sanctum.
Ah... General Huaiyan's gone. Wait, why does something feel off about what we talked about!?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I agree. General Feixiao is indeed impressive.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I agree. General Feixiao is indeed impressive.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Can't you put a little more enthusiasm into it?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Thanks for the kind words, Miss March. The Wardance is coming up, and I've been chosen to represent the Cloud Knights in the ceremony.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: I bet it's about how to deal with the generals from the Yaoqing and the Zhuming.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The Marshal is well aware of Jing Yuan's purpose in holding the ceremony and understands the situation he is facing. She mentioned it because she believes both issues are important.
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: No need for that. You're all important witnesses. The Marshal is well aware of Jing Yuan's purpose in holding the ceremony and understands the situation he is facing. She mentioned it because she believes both issues are important.
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: Thanks for your kindness and sincerity, Elder Huaiyan, but is it appropriate... to tell everyone here about the Marshal's orders?
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Not to be rude or anything... We've been watching their drama. I'm dying to find out who beats who.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Things are already complicated enough as they are, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Your talent is quite... unique. Are you also interested in swordplay?
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: Isn't this a perfect chance for you? I remember you mentioning that you wanted to learn some sword moves.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I appreciate your kind words, General Huaiyan. But won't teaching me swordplay be a waste of Yanqing and Yunli's time? They should be preparing for the ceremony.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: At least that way, I won't have to worry about you accidentally shooting me in the butt all the time.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Yeah, while I'm smart, learning swordplay sounds like a whole lot of work.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I understand.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Then I'm on board! Thank you for your kindness, General Huaiyan.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: But from his point of view, we're no different from all the other tourists who may leave at any time.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Don't worry, General. No matter what happens, I'm prepared to stay here as the Express' witness, and answer any questions.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Did we do something wrong? We really did save the Luofu, so why do you want to sneak off like we're fugitives?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Thank you, everyone.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Hey, was that the Yaoqing General who just dropped in out of nowhere? She's so awesome!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I mean, when Yunli swung that massive sword, she just casually blocked her attack with ease...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...And mine, too.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Ahem, yeah... But to go up against Yunli is quite impressive, you know? That aura of heroism and grace. It almost makes me want to learn Xianzhou swordplay!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You think so too, right, [Trailblazer]?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Uh... I was talking about Yanqing, actually.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I was actually hoping you'd give Yanqing some praise!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I've had my fair share of defeats lately, and even though I know there are always more skilled swordmasters out there, seeing General Feixiao's skills today has made me feel a bit uneasy again.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Don't underestimate yourself. After all, generals won't fight in the ring during the Wardance. Just remember the state of mind you had when you single-handedly took on me and Blade, putting life and death aside. With that mindset, you can prevail against most challengers.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I see. Thanks for the advice, Master Dan Heng! By the way, now that today's events are over, General Jing Yuan wants to invite all of you to the Seat of Divine Foresight. He has something important to discuss.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: *sigh* I really don't want to get caught up in grown-up games so soon... I just hope Generals Feixiao and Huaiyan can see the truth. We don't need any more chaos on the Luofu before the Wardance.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: The Marshal ordered me to come to the Xianzhou Luofu, but the document only says: "Attend the Wardance and listen to Feixiao's questioning."
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: By introducing the Express' witnesses to me alone, aren't you aiming to discern the intentions behind both my actions and Feixiao's, and whether there's any discord between us? Well, since I'm being open and honest with you, I encourage you young folk to do the same.
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: As for the Ambrosial Arbor Crisis, all I need to do is listen. General Feixiao will be the one asking the questions. To be honest, I'm more concerned about the timely start of the Wardance.
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: Oh, by the way, I've prepared a gift for the Wardance.
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: Uh... I think we strayed off topic. How did things even get to this point?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Yeah, I brought you here because the general said he had some important matters to discuss. But how in the world... did Yunli and I suddenly become Miss March's swordplay mentors?
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Because... General Huaiyan wants us to stick around on the Luofu for some time.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Since the Crew's actions were mentioned in the Luofu's operations log that was given to the Alliance, he probably wants to see firsthand if we're as capable as the report claims, or if we're just some made-up excuse to save face.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: And he wants to see it for himself during the Wardance, which is why he even dragged Yunli into this. What began as a simple contest between two swordmasters... has now evolved into you two collaborating to mentor March.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Elder Huaiyan is still that tricky general who likes to give everyone a headache.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Earlier at the Palace of Astrum, I introduced these guests from the Astral Express to you, Elder Huaiyan, but with all the people around, we only exchanged pleasantries. Now, I'd like to officially introduce them to you.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: These three braved great dangers, accompanying me to perilous places, defeating the chief culprit Phantylia, and uncovering the conspiracies of the Disciples of Sanctus Medicus. If you wish to know more, please feel free to ask us.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Well, I skimmed through the reports about the Arbor's rebirth from the Master Diviner Fu Xuan. She's been summoned to the Yuque for questioning. There are a lot of doubts within the Alliance about this whole situation...
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: ...But despite all that, I believe in you.
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: Since you joined the ranks, you have repeatedly achieved remarkable feats. After the High-Cloud Quintet each went their separate ways, despite the many criticisms within the Alliance, the Marshal still stood firm against the dissenting voices, and entrusted the Luofu to you.
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: Over the years, you've served the Alliance with loyalty and wisdom. You've taken down abominations in Thalassa, rescued the Xianzhou Yuque from a siege, and destroyed the demonic planet summoned by the Denizens of Abundance... I still remember those battles vividly.
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: There are fools who doubt your loyalty. They're happy to see the Divine Foresight fail because it gives them some kind of sick satisfaction. They haven't achieved anything of their own, so they feed off the failures of others.
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: But I've seen enough failures in my time. And I want to believe that your loyalty has never wavered.
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: So, General Feixiao of the Yaoqing is the only one investigating the Ambrosial Arbor Crisis on behalf of the Alliance?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: No, no. I am, too.
rows.speaker: Huaiyan

rows.text: This old man's words... always catch me off guard.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: My apologies. Truth be told, I invited all of you to the ceremony because I wished for you to act as my witnesses. I apologize for not disclosing this information earlier.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: In the coming weeks, I'll also invite all of you to a meeting with General Feixiao, where you may need to answer her questions and clear up any doubts she might have. So, please be prepared for the meeting.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Don't worry, [Trailblazer]. No matter what happens, I'll stay here as a witness and answer any questions she might have.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: General! I know there isn't much I can do to share your burden, but...
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Hm?
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: As the Luofu ringmaster, I won't let anyone defeat me in the Wardance!
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: I know.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: I'm still feeling sleepy...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Hmm, did I oversleep? Where did March and Dan Heng go?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: There you are, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Why are you here too, Yanqing?
What kind of master waits on their apprentice's doorstep?
March? Show some respect to your master.
You haven't forgotten about our promise to General Huaiyan, have you? I woke up especially early, so I could start teaching Miss March swordplay.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Well, it was a promise to General Huaiyan, after all. I woke up especially early, so I could start teaching Miss March swordplay.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: It's an honor to learn from you, Master Yanqing!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: In all those immersias and novels I watched, when apprentices want to pay their respects to their masters, they usually bring fancy gifts, kneel, and bow. I'm really sorry, but I haven't prepared anything yet.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hey, why are you blushing, Master Yanqing?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: This is the first time someone has called me master... I need to... get used to it...
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Let me make it clear: Swordplay training is about improving your body, mind, and strength. It's not a casual game you can master overnight.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: I promised General Huaiyan that I'd teach you Cloud Knight swordplay, so you can participate in the Wardance and defeat at least one opponent. I'll do my best, but if you break your master's rules...
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Wh—what will you do?
March is always a good girl!
Is it too late for regrets? I'm already regretting my impulsive decision.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Honestly, I'm not sure what I'll do either, because I've never been a teacher before. So, Miss March, please behave and don't skip classes or complain.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: You need to toughen up and train her properly, Master Yanqing. Don't go easy on her.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: You're so heartless, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Fine. A promise is a promise. Since I promised to study hard, I'll do my best starting today!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Great! That's the spirit.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: March is in your hands now, Yanqing. Don't be too easy on her.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Dan Heng, do you even have a heart? Did you lose it somewhere?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: By the way, where's Yunli?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I've found a quiet spot in the back garden of the Palace of Astrum for our first lesson together.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: March 7th waves to you and Dan Heng, embarking on the first lesson of her sword training journey...
Seriously? It's the first day, and you two are already late? Why is everyone on the Luofu so laid-back? So disappointing.
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: I'm ready...
Not really...
Ah, Master Yunli you're already here. Sorry for keeping you waiting!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Wait, were you trying to teach her in secret? That's sneaky!
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: I'm just showing you what Luofu etiquette is all about. She might be my apprentice, but it's customary for the master to personally escort their apprentice to the place of learning.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: As the host, I'll be teaching Miss March the essence of Luofu swordplay, after which she'll emerge victorious in the Wardance ring. You won't be complaining about Luofu swordplay then!
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Stand aside, rookie. Let me show you how we Zhuming swordmasters treat their apprentices.
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: Quickly, over here, Miss March. This is a "reverse mentorship gift" from me to you. I hope you put it to good use.
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: What's this... Xianzhou clothing? It's so beautiful!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Sword practice requires precise movements. This outfit is tailored to fit perfectly and allows for smooth movements. I even added some small accessories. I put a lot of thought into it.
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: You're awesome, Master Yunli!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: See? See? How can you compete with me? I'll teach March 7th the essence of Zhuming swordplay, so she can win the contest with my sword skills.
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: Actually, I've prepared something too.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Huh? You have a gift for me too, Master Yanqing?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Since you want to learn swordplay, Miss March, you'll need suitable weapons. So, I went out of my way to prepare a pair of swords overnight.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Unfortunately, I didn't have time to ask the craftsman to customize the swords for you, but I did my best to choose ones that look nice and are suitable for a beginner. I hope you like them, Miss March.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Thank you, Master Yanqing!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Bet you didn't see that coming, did you, Yunli?
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Hmph, the real competition is just getting started.
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: I'm so lucky to have two great masters! But why does it feel like things are getting a bit weird?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Thus begins the journey of March 7th's sword training.
Time marches on, and days turn to more...
I've been watching your progress during this period! How about another spar?
rows.speaker: Cloud Knight Instructor

rows.text: Bring it on.
Next time.
Bring it on! Let's see how I beat you this time!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That's the spirit!
rows.speaker: Cloud Knight Instructor

rows.text: Maybe next time. I've got something else to do now.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: No problem! I'm ready whenever you need me.
rows.speaker: Cloud Knight Instructor

rows.text: So, what do you think, masters? Does this outfit suit me?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Perfect! I chose it carefully — it's perfect for beautiful young swordswomen like you and me!
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: Alright, let's get started with the training. The person next to me is a Cloud Knight instructor I've brought in. For your first lesson, try exchanging a couple of moves with him.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Wait, we're having actual combat training for the first lesson!? Isn't that a bit too intense?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Well, I heard you have some experience with archery and martial arts. The first thing we're going to do is see just how strong your fundamentals are.
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: (Oh come on, March 7th! Really now? You just got into swordplay training. Are you sick of it already? Is that why you want to skip practice?)
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: (No, both my masters will be mad if I do that...)
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: After a day of running around, you finally arrive at Petrichor Inn for a well-deserved rest...
This night, your restlessness from meeting the general and the bustling crowd before the Wardance keeps you from falling asleep.
Day two.

Come on, step forward and strike with the sword in the most natural way you can think of! It's important for us to grasp your natural movements, so we can decide where to start and what you need to learn.
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: If you're ready, let's begin!
rows.speaker: Cloud Knight Instructor

rows.text: Ah... haha... okay...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Are you ready?
rows.speaker: Cloud Knight Instructor

rows.text: Yeah, I'm ready... but please go easy on me!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Then I apologize in advance, Miss March!
rows.speaker: Cloud Knight Instructor

rows.text: I need some more time to prepare myself...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Let's go now!
No rush! Take your time!
rows.speaker: Cloud Knight Instructor

rows.text: I didn't expect the first lesson to be so intense...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Miss March has quick hands and a flexible body. She's a perfect fit for practicing Luofu swordplay.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: However, she lacks strength, and her strikes were a bit unfocused... but don't worry, that's totally normal for beginners. Once she starts practicing Zhuming swordplay, she'll make heaps of progress.
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: Given the situation, I believe Miss March should start by working on —
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Her footwork. Her strength.
rows.speaker: Yanqing & Yunli

rows.text: Seriously, do you actually know anything about swordplay or what?
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: I tried to drag [Trailblazer] into this, but {F#she}{M#he} refused. Then I tried to rope Dan Heng in, but Master Yanqing wouldn't have it.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I could ask you the same thing! Dual swords require agility, so what's more important than footwork?
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Instead of focusing on her strengths, we should address her weaknesses. The drawback of wielding two swords is not generating enough force. What good is being quick on your feet if you don't have strength? It's not like we're dancing here.
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: Skilled swordmasters know how to play to their strengths and work on their weaknesses. Start with what you're good at, then tackle your weaknesses. That's the right way to learn.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Days and nights fly by in the delve, as the Wardance fast approaches.
Under the strict supervision of her two masters, March 7th trains tirelessly, almost developing tennis elbow.
On that day, after the sword training...
You're quite the theorist, huh?
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: Theorist? You claim to be able to talk to swords, so what does that make you? A lunatic?
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Hey, it's only my first lesson, and you're already arguing! Come on, calm down, masters! I'll have to improve both my footwork and strength anyway, so it doesn't matter which one comes first!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: But it does matter!!! Just listen to me, March 7th!
rows.speaker: Yanqing & Yunli

rows.text: Dear Himeko, Mr. Yang, and Pom-Pom, We're all good here on the Xianzhou Luofu, so no need to worry! By the way, how's your trip going?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: As for me, I've somehow become the apprentice to two Cloud Knight swordmasters, and I've been honing my sword skills with their guidance.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: One of them is Yanqing, the boy we've all met before. The other is Yunli, the granddaughter of General Huaiyan from the Xianzhou Zhuming.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Both masters are super strict, giving me a real taste of how hard sword training can be.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Still, I didn't let the difficulty get to me. In just a few weeks, my sword skills have improved a lot. Both my masters think I have unique talents in swordplay and are literally fighting each other to teach me their skills.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Thanks to their guidance, I've actually made some progress. When I get back to the Express, I'll definitely show off my skills and impress you all!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Looking forward to your reply. Yours, March 7th.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Well done. Let's call it a day.
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: Miss March's sword skills are really coming along. She'll hold her own just fine in the Wardance.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Perhaps... I might have a shot at beating both masters in the ring?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Get real, you've only been practicing for a short while. How could that possibly happen?
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: With your talent, Miss March, if you dedicate a few more decades to training, you might eventually be able to defeat Yunli.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Bah!
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: Decades...? But I'll be an old lady by then... No, no.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Just you wait and see! I'll show off my skills in the ring and win a match. I'll make both of you proud!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Can you believe it? March 7th has actually become a pretty decent swordmaster in such a short time. Now I understand why grandpa always had a grin on his face while training me.
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: Are you sure he wasn't laughing at you?
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Shut up!
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: It's all thanks to your amazing guidance, masters!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Miss March, you're really getting the hang of wielding dual swords. If you're keen on advancing, trying out different Xianzhou blades could improve your touch.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Hmm, let me see... Which sword is the most powerful? Single sword? Greatsword? Or maybe a flying sword?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: There's no such thing as the "most powerful" sword. It's all about the skill of the swordmaster. Yanqing wields several flying swords, while I only wield one, but remember how I kicked his butt at the Alchemy Commission?
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: First, you didn't kick my butt! Second, you'll never kick my butt! Third, how about we settle this right now and see who kicks whose butt?
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Yeah, I'm up for that! And if I kick your butt, you'll drop out of the Wardance. Deal?
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: Why are you two arguing again? I thought things had been improving between you lately...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: There was talk that the leading disciples of the Luofu and Zhuming generals were supposed to face off in the Wardance, but for some reason, they suddenly teamed up to train an apprentice of their own. Turns out the rumors are true.
rows.speaker: Jiaoqiu

rows.text: Tomorrow is the big day of the Wardance. Shouldn't you two be focusing on honing your skills instead of teaching swordplay here?
rows.speaker: Jiaoqiu

rows.text: Ah, you're... um, you're... That's right! You're the pink-haired fox from the Yaoqing!
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: This is Mr. Jiaoqiu, the healer working for the General of the Xianzhou Yaoqing.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hahaha...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: What are you laughing at? You've got pink-hair, too!
rows.speaker: Jiaoqiu

rows.text: I'm Jiaoqiu, the healer working for the General of the Xianzhou Yaoqing.
rows.speaker: Jiaoqiu

rows.text: Ah, got it. So, you're the participant attending the Wardance on behalf of the Yaoqing, and you were trying to sneak a peek at our training?
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: Sorry for the misunderstanding. I don't know anything about martial arts. I'm just here on the general's orders to take care of some official business. I didn't mean to interrupt your training. I'll be on my way.
rows.speaker: Jiaoqiu

rows.text: If you know nothing about martial arts, why were you smirking earlier?
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: Well, my curiosity got the better of me I suppose. When I heard Miss March's pondering about what to learn, I couldn't help but wander over.
rows.speaker: Jiaoqiu

rows.text: From my professional experience, cleavers, slicers, chopping knives, and carving knives are all just tools, kind of like frying, sautéing, boiling, and deep-frying in cooking. They're just ways for people to show off their skills. How you use them really depends on the ingredients you're working with.
rows.speaker: Jiaoqiu

rows.text: It's like your sword teaching methods. If you align your "ingredient" — in other words your apprentice's natural tendencies with the right "cooking method" — by which I mean the teaching method that best suits her, she'll make double the progress in half the time!
rows.speaker: Jiaoqiu

rows.text: For example, Golden Eggplant tastes best when fried, Cloud Peppers when stir-fried, and Yellow Boulder Beef when simmered. It's all about discovering the nature of the ingredients... uh, I mean, apprentice.
rows.speaker: Jiaoqiu

rows.text: All this talk about food is making me hungry.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Aren't you a healer? Why are you talking about food?
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: Well, it's just a metaphor. The medicinal school I follow on the Xianzhou Yaoqing is called the Ranzhi School, that specializes in food therapy, so it's only natural that I know a thing or two about cooking.
rows.speaker: Jiaoqiu

rows.text: So... you're the general's cook?
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: I'm a healer! But anyway, a cook who isn't interested in health doesn't make for a good advisor. Fine, call me a cook if you want.
rows.speaker: Jiaoqiu

rows.text: Seeing the way you're looking at me, it's obvious you think I'm just some feeble academic who likes to blabber on about martial arts. But in reality, I know a thing or two about killing. After all, the art of healing inherently encompasses both life and death.
rows.speaker: Jiaoqiu

rows.text: Why is this guy suddenly getting all serious with kids?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Seriously, trying to save face in front of kids? *sigh*
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Do you recognize this bottle of medicine in my hand?
rows.speaker: Jiaoqiu

rows.text: No.
rows.speaker: Yanqing & Yunli & March 7th

rows.text: This is called "Tumbledust"! An extract from an exotic flower named "Yabruh."
rows.speaker: Jiaoqiu

rows.text: Moments later
Is it poison?
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Well, it depends on how it's used. With just one drop, it's able to numb a patient's body during surgery, making them painless throughout the entire process. However...
rows.speaker: Jiaoqiu

rows.text: Increase the dose or the potency, and it'll slow the metabolism, making the blood thin and resulting in the loss of all senses. Even long-life species cannot escape its effects.
rows.speaker: Jiaoqiu

rows.text: This thing can save lives or take them. It's more powerful than the swords in your hands.
rows.speaker: Jiaoqiu

rows.text: That may be so, but still I prefer settling things with a sword than... you know...
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: Looks like I did get you all wrong. You're not a feeble scholar, but a sinister and despicable one.
rows.speaker: Yunli

rows.text: Hey, hey, why the insults all of a sudden? I'm just sharing some medical knowledge here, not persuading you to poison anyone.
rows.speaker: Jiaoqiu

rows.text: Seems like you get real excited when talking about poison. I can't tell if that's an honorable thing or sinister...
